text: Barley failed across the Tavrin Valley this season, according to the valley’s Crop Board, which said early frost and a dry April cut yields to 28% of normal. The board’s August tally put average output at 0.7 tonnes per hectare, down from 2.5 tonnes a year earlier. Agronomist Elin Voss said the loss hit 14 cooperatives, with 3,900 hectares written off after heads never filled properly. Grain buyers in the nearby Sorell market have already lifted forward bids 11% on replacement supply. For the sector, the failure tightens feed stocks and is likely to push millers toward imported grain, while leaving malt houses with a thinner local pipeline through winter.
